author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 길잃은새, 지금까지 기록 10건 미만 · 2000년 이후 확인된 기록 없음

months.note: 국내에서 기록된 달(1888년 2월 원산 부근, 1912년 12월 충남 예산)이며, 번식지에서는 4~6월에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 늪과 해변, 탁 트인 땅에서 지내는 새이다. 국내에서는 충청남도와 함경남도에서 보인 적이 있으나, 지금까지 기록이 10건이 안 되는 길잃은새이다. 홀로 지내며 땅 위나 언덕, 바위, 말뚝에 가만히 앉아 가까이 나타나는 먹이를 기다린다. 쥐, 두더지, 새, 족제비, 곤충 따위를 잡아먹는다. 시베리아, 알래스카, 캐나다, 스칸디나비아반도에 분포하며, 번식지에서는 4~6월에 무늬 없는 흰 알을 낳는다.

points.en: blackish-brown markings on back, flight-feather tips and tail

points.ko: 깃이 빽빽한 다리와 발가락, 검은 발톱
points.en: densely feathered legs and toes, black claws

sexes.female: 날개 길이가 약 45cm로 수컷보다 몸집이 크고, 등 쪽에 검은 갈색 가로무늬가 있다.

young: 첫겨울 어린새는 수컷도 어른 암컷처럼 갈색 가로무늬가 많고, 어린 암컷은 가로무늬가 더 굵고 촘촘해 가장 어둡게 보인다. 갓 둥지를 떠난 새끼는 짙은 회갈색 깃에 얼굴만 희다.

art.subject: Snowy Owl (Bubo scandiacus), adult male in winter: almost pure white all over, with only a few small, sparse blackish-brown spots and bars on the back, the tips of the flight feathers and the tail, and a few fine dark flecks on the crown and nape. Round head with no visible ear-tufts and a white face without a sharply rimmed facial disc. Black bill, largely hidden in the white facial feathers; bright golden-yellow eyes; legs and toes buried in dense white feathering, black claws.
art.pose: sitting still on a wooden post, watching the ground for prey
art.scene: Korean winter open country: a coastal marsh beside a beach with dry grass and a lone post; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched upright: almost pure white, a few small blackish-brown spots on the back, flight-feather tips and tail, round head without ear-tufts, black bill half hidden, yellow eyes, thickly feathered white feet

adult female, side view perched upright: larger and bulkier, white face and throat, crown, nape and neck finely marked dark, back, wings and tail heavily barred blackish brown, breast sides, belly and flanks also barred, yellow eyes
foot detail: short legs and toes buried in dense white feathering like fur, only the curved black claws showing
art.build: Large, bulky, heavy-bodied owl, much bigger than a crow and close to a Eurasian Eagle-Owl in size; females clearly larger than males. Big rounded head set flush on a broad body, no neck visible. Bill short, strongly hooked, black, mostly buried in facial feathering. Legs short and so thickly feathered that the feet look like white fur mittens with black claws. Wings long and broad; tail short and rounded. Sits upright and still on the ground, a mound or a post; flight low with steady, rather shallow wingbeats.
avoid: Do not paint ear-tufts; the Snowy Owl's head is smoothly round (ear-tufts mark the Eurasian Eagle-Owl).
Do not paint orange, red or dark eyes; the iris is bright yellow.
Do not give it a heart-shaped facial disc like a Barn Owl, or bare yellow toes.
Do not cover the adult male in dense dark barring; heavy barring belongs to females and young birds.
